In [[algebraic topology]] and [[category theory]], '''factorization homology''' is a variant of [[topological chiral homology]], motivated by an application to [[topological quantum field theory]] and [[cobordism hypothesis]] in particular. It was introduced by David Ayala, John Francis, and Nick Rozenblyum.<ref>{{cite journal
| last=Ayala | first=David
| last2=Francis | first2=John
| last3=Rozenblyum | first3=Nick
| title=Factorization homology I: Higher categories
| arxiv=1504.04007
| journal=[[Advances in Mathematics]]
| volume=333
| year=2018
| pages=1042–1177
| mr=3818096
| doi=10.1016/j.aim.2018.05.031 | doi-access=free}}</ref>
